Load the per-tick state table of a run

Source: R/load.R
load_state.Rd

Reads state.tsv, by default its host rows. A mosquito's row counts the lineages it carries, so a prevalence or MOI taken over every row mixes the two populations. Every run gives the same 12 columns, in the order and classes the model writes them (state.tsv describes them), whatever the run holds; a column the file lacks is NA.

Usage

load_state(run, entity = c("human", "mosquito", "all"))

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

entity

the rows to give: "human" (the hosts), "mosquito", or "all", both in the order of the file.

Value

a data.table with one row per host (or mosquito, or both) per day, from day 1 to the run's last day.

Examples

st <- load_state(example_run())
st[tick == 400]   # every host on the last day
#>      tick entity_type entity_id   tag moi_active moi_subpatent moi_dormant
